title: Iterated macrosteps track the source run
statement: Let $W$ and $M$ be finite binary Turing machines, let $a,B\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $x$ be a binary word with $|x|+1\le B$. Suppose a schedule configuration has its unary tape equal to the unary tape with $B$ markers and its guide tape equal to the fixed guide of radius $3B$. Suppose also that data tapes encode the head-centered payload vectors of the initial configuration of $M$ on $x$. For every $j\le B$, there are read and neighbor-register vectors and new data tapes such that after $j(18B+8)$ simulator steps from the macrostep-check configuration with unary head at $1$, the simulator is again at the macrostep-check phase with unary head at $j+1$, its state and saved bit equal the state and last output bit (defaulting to false) of the $j$-step run of $M$ on $x$, and the new data tapes encode the head-centered payload vectors of that run.
hypotheses_covered: base unary tape equals the unary tape with $B$ markers
base guide tape equals the guide of radius $3B$
initial data tapes decode to the source payloads of $M$ on $x$
replaced:
Let the base configuration's unary tape have $B$ markers with $|x| + 1 \le B$
and its guide tape have radius $3B$, and let the data tapes decode the
head-centered payload vectors of the initial configuration of the source $M$ on
$x$.  Then for every $j \le B$ there are reads, neighbor registers, and data
tapes such that $j\,(18B + 8)$ simulator steps from the first counter-test
configuration reach the counter-test phase with unary head $j + 1$, carrying the
state and last-emitted bit of the $j$-step run of $M$ on $x$, with data tapes
decoding that run's head-centered payload vectors and no output emitted.
